newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF's Sakakibara says Japan forex policy unchanged.
newsitem.headline: MOF's Sakakibara says Japan forex policy unchanged.

text.p: Eisuke Sakakibara, a key official of Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF), said on Tuesday that there has been no change in the ministry's policy on foreign exchange.
Sakakibara, who has been appointed vice minister of international affairs at the Ministry of Finance (MOF), told Reuters in a telephone interview : "The MOF's forex policy has not changed".
"As with the U.S. Treasury, (the MOF) does not have any intention at all of using foreign exchange rates as an instrument of trade policy," Sakakibara added.
The dollar rose above 113 yen following the remarks. It was traded at around 112.50 yen before the comments were reported.

On Monday, the dollar had slipped against the yen after the release of data showing a sharp rise in Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus for the June 1-20 period, which fuelled worries about Tokyo's growing trade surplus.
